nodes.content: Develop a subsurface two-phase flow surrogate that preserves local mass conservation while generalizing across unseen permeability connectivity.
requirements: Maximum cellwise mass-balance error stays below 0.1% of injected mass per timestep.
On unseen channel connectivity, breakthrough-time error remains below 5% versus a converged finite-volume solver.

nodes.content: Train a permeability-conditioned graph network to predict transmissibility corrections, then solve pressure and update saturations using shared-face finite-volume phase fluxes.
Shared-face fluxes keep cellwise imbalance below 0.1% of injected mass per step; graph-conditioned corrections keep unseen-connectivity breakthrough error below 5%.
Benchmark 200 held-out channel-connectivity realizations against converged finite-volume solutions, measuring maximum per-step injected-mass-normalized cellwise imbalance and breakthrough-time error.
Across 200 held-out channel realizations, maximum per-step normalized cellwise imbalance was 0.06%, and worst-case breakthrough-time error was 4.2%.
Can permeability-conditioned graph corrections resolve unseen dead-end channels adjacent to injection wells at 100:1 permeability contrast?
Using the 200-realization benchmark as baseline, test added 100:1 near-well dead ends against finite-volume breakthrough and mass-balance metrics.
Generate 80 unseen 100:1 near-well dead-end channels; compare surrogate breakthrough times and maximum normalized cellwise imbalance against finite-volume solutions.
DeadEnd-80 benchmark: 80 held-out 100:1 near-well channel maps, converged finite-volume trajectories, and per-case breakthrough and cellwise-imbalance scores.
Validate DeadEnd-80 finite-volume convergence and score surrogate breakthrough error and normalized cellwise imbalance by dead-end length and well distance.
On DeadEnd-80, maximum normalized cellwise imbalance was 0.07%; worst-case breakthrough-time error versus converged finite-volume solutions was 4.6%.
On 120 unseen braided-channel maps, ablate graph-conditioned transmissibility corrections and shared-face updates; compare breakthrough error and maximum cellwise imbalance.
On 120 unseen braided maps, worst-case breakthrough-time error reached 9.1% versus finite-volume solutions despite 0.08% maximum normalized cellwise imbalance.
Does limited graph message-passing radius miss competing parallel pathways in unseen braided channels, causing 9.1% worst-case breakthrough error?
Using DeadEnd-80 success and braided-channel failure as controls, sweep graph message-passing radii and measure breakthrough error against finite-volume references.
Retrain 2-, 4-, 8-, and 16-hop networks identically; compare breakthrough errors on 120 braided maps and DeadEnd-80.
HopSweep-v1 contains four matched network checkpoints, predictions on 120 braided maps and DeadEnd-80, and per-case breakthrough-error tables.
Add multiscale well-to-well pathway attention to transmissibility corrections while retaining pressure solves and shared-face finite-volume fluxes.
Multiscale pathway attention reduces worst-case braided-channel breakthrough error below 5% without raising normalized cellwise imbalance above 0.1%.
Select HopSweep-v1's lowest-error checkpoint, add multiscale well-to-well attention, and measure braided/DeadEnd-80 breakthrough errors and cellwise imbalance versus finite-volume references.
On 120 braided maps, pathway attention achieved 4.3% worst-case breakthrough error and 0.08% maximum normalized cellwise imbalance.
Benchmark pathway attention against HopSweep-v1 checkpoints on 100 new 100:1 braided maps, tracking worst-case breakthrough error and cellwise imbalance.
On 100 new 100:1 braided maps, pathway attention reached 7.4% worst-case breakthrough error despite 0.09% maximum normalized cellwise imbalance.
Does pathway attention misrank competing high-contrast branches when pressure gradients redirect flow, explaining the 7.4% worst-case breakthrough error?
Compare attention branch rankings with finite-volume fluxes in 120-map and 100-map cohorts, stratifying pressure reversals and breakthrough errors.
Audit pathway-attention rankings against finite-volume branch fluxes across both braided cohorts, stratifying pressure reversals, breakthrough error, and cellwise imbalance.
In 100 high-contrast maps, attention misranked dominant branches during 28% of pressure reversals; worst-case breakthrough error reached 7.4%.
Recomputing pathway attention from each pressure solve will reduce high-contrast branch misranking below 10% and worst-case breakthrough error below 5%.
Using the audited 100-map cohort, recompute attention after each pressure solve; measure branch misranking, worst-case breakthrough error, and cellwise imbalance.
Across 100 maps, pressure-updated attention cut branch misranking to 8% and worst-case breakthrough error to 4.7%; maximum imbalance was 0.09%.
Adopt pressure-updated pathway attention: 4.3% braided error warranted retention; 7.4% high-contrast failure and 28% misranking required updating; revised error 4.7%.
Use topology-aware multigrid pressure prediction with locally conservative fine-grid phase-flux reconstruction and finite-volume saturation updates.
Topology-aware multigrid resolves nonlocal braided pathways, yielding worst-case breakthrough error below 5% and maximum normalized cellwise imbalance below 0.1%.
Train topology-aware multigrid on matched realizations; benchmark both braided cohorts against converged finite-volume references for worst-case breakthrough error and imbalance.
Across both braided cohorts, multigrid's worst-case breakthrough error was 4.8% versus converged finite-volume references; maximum normalized cellwise imbalance was 0.08%.
Benchmark multigrid on 96 unseen branching-channel maps at 200:1 permeability contrast against converged finite-volume breakthrough times and cellwise mass balance.
On 96 unseen 200:1 branching maps, multigrid reached 8.3% worst-case breakthrough error despite 0.08% maximum normalized cellwise imbalance.
Does coarse-grid aggregation erase narrow 200:1 branches, causing multigrid's 8.3% worst-case breakthrough error despite conservative flux reconstruction?
Contrast successful braided and failing 200:1 branching cohorts; vary aggregation scale and measure narrow-branch flux loss and breakthrough error.
Reaggregate braided and 200:1 branching maps at 2×2, 4×4, and 8×8 scales; compare narrow-branch flux retention and breakthrough errors.
On 200:1 branching maps, 8×8 aggregates retained 62% of reference narrow-branch flux versus 94% at 2×2; breakthrough error reached 8.3%.
Defer 8×8 multigrid: braided error was 4.8%, but branching error reached 8.3% with only 62% narrow-branch flux retention.
Combine pressure-updated pathway attention with branch-preserving adaptive multigrid pressure solves and shared-face finite-volume phase fluxes.
Adaptive branch-preserving solves plus pressure-updated attention achieve under 5% worst-case breakthrough error and 0.1% maximum normalized cellwise imbalance.
Benchmark hybrid on both held-out high-contrast cohorts, measuring worst-case breakthrough error and maximum injected-mass-normalized cellwise imbalance against finite-volume references.
Across 100 braided and 96 branching high-contrast maps, hybrid worst-case breakthrough error was 4.5%; maximum normalized cellwise imbalance was 0.08%.
Building on the hybrid's 196-map results, benchmark 300 unseen channel topologies against converged finite-volume breakthrough and cellwise mass balance.
Generate 300 unseen 50:1–200:1 connected, braided, and branching maps; run converged finite-volume references and hybrid predictions.
Connectivity-300 contains 300 held-out permeability maps, converged finite-volume trajectories, hybrid predictions, and per-case breakthrough and mass-balance scores.
Validate Connectivity-300 reference convergence; audit hybrid worst-case breakthrough error and per-step maximum normalized cellwise imbalance by topology.
On Connectivity-300, hybrid worst-case breakthrough-time error was 4.7% versus converged finite-volume references; maximum normalized cellwise imbalance was 0.09%.
Select the hybrid for deployment: Connectivity-300 worst-case breakthrough error was 4.7% and maximum cellwise imbalance 0.09%, confirming high-contrast results.
